# finport-ratesengine

> A deterministic SOFR rates engine that reports the evidence behind a number,
> not just the number. Every curve says which instruments pinned it and what
> each one's repricing residual was; every price says which curve discounted
> it and why that curve; every risk figure says which bump basis and shape
> produced it, and every degradation along the way — a Treasury par yield
> standing in for an OIS quote, a contract notional nobody verified — travels
> up the chain to the result that rests on it.

Install `finport-ratesengine`, import `rates_engine`, run `rateng`. The three
names differ because the obvious distribution name follows the convention of
its sibling project. Python 3.11+. MIT.

The core install is numpy, pandas and scipy, and nothing else. YAML configs
for the CLI are the one extra (`config`); JSON configs are native precisely so
that a core install can run every command.

Two ways in. As a library, importing `rates_engine`. As a CLI, `rateng`, where
`bootstrap`, `price`, `hedge` and `describe` take `--json` and put one
parseable document on stdout with all narration on stderr. An MCP server is
planned for v2.

## What it does

Builds an OIS-SOFR discount curve from a realised stub, SOFR futures adjusted
for convexity, and par quotes; exposes it as discount factors, zero rates, par
rates and forwards, each carrying the compounding basis and day count that
make it mean something. Prices OIS, fixed-versus-Term-SOFR IRS and FRAs under
collateral discounting, with the projection curve and the discount curve kept
apart. Measures risk: parallel DV01, a key-rate profile built from tent shocks
that sum exactly to a parallel shift, PVBP, money duration, money convexity,
and the effective measures where the price is not zero. Sizes a futures strip
against a swap and shocks the hedged position, so the convexity the strip
cannot hedge shows up in dollars and in basis points.

## What it refuses

A missing fixing is never interpolated. An unimplemented convention never
falls back to a default. A Treasury par yield never enters a curve without
being declared. A key rate is never extrapolated past the curve. A duration is
never divided by a zero price. Macaulay and modified duration are never
approximated by effective duration under their own names. Seventeen named
exceptions, each with an exit code and an entry in `docs/ERRORS.md` saying
whether it is recoverable and what to do.

## What it is not

Not an agent and not a model. No LLM is invoked from the library, and no
token is spent at runtime. There is no randomness: the same input on the same
interpreter gives the same output bit for bit, and across interpreter versions
to 1e-14 relative.

Not a volatility engine. Swaptions, caps, floors and the SABR cube are v2.
Not multi-currency: TIIE, FX forwards and FX options are v3. No CVA, FVA, KVA
or MVA; no CCP margin; no SA-CCR. Clean prices only.

## Honest limits in v1

The dual-curve solver is validated against synthetic inputs, because no free
source of Term SOFR par or basis swap quotes exists; every such result
declares `inputs_origin="synthetic"`. The long end can use Treasury par
yields as a proxy for OIS par, which carries a swap spread that is negative,
variable and not quantified here — it is opt-in, it marks every node it
touches, and it is barred from any test that validates a published number. The
SR1 contract notional is assumed rather than read from the contract spec, and
the evidence says `notional_source="assumed"`.
